note: Reward-noise variant of the control experiment, frozen before any training run of this variant. Single change versus the control: zero-mean Gaussian noise added to the reward the agent receives (and stores in replay) at every env step. Environment, starts, budget, network, hyperparameters and seeds are copied unchanged; the only difference between the two algorithms is still agent.doubleQ. One pass of 6 runs; no tuning and no selective rerun after seeing results. If a run fails for a technical reason, the bug fix is documented here and all 6 runs are redone. Results must come from the raw JSONL logs; do not edit numbers after the run.

task.description: 1-D navigation on [0, 1]. Action 1 = +0.15, action 0 = -0.15. Episode ends at position > 0.7 or 25 steps. Reward +1 on success else -0.05 per step.
task.start: uniform[0, 0.4] via mulberry32(seed * 1009), as in RL 1
task.success: episode terminated by reaching position > 0.7 before the 25-step limit

rewardNoise.appliedTo: the reward passed to agent.remember() at every env step (training only); the environment, its termination and the true reward are unchanged
rewardNoise.stream: own seeded stream, independent of env starts, exploration and replay sampling: mulberry32(seed * 7919 + 101), one standard normal per env step by Box-Muller (two uniforms per draw, cosine branch). The k-th env step of a run receives the same noise draw for dqn and double-dqn at equal seed.
rewardNoise.sigmaJustification: Set from the reward function alone, no trial run: rewards are +1 on success and -0.05 otherwise. Under the optimal policy (always +0.15) from starts uniform[0, 0.4], episodes last 3, 4 or 5 steps (probabilities 0.375, 0.375, 0.25; 3.875 steps on average), so the pooled per-step reward has mean 0.221 and standard deviation 0.459 (exact, from nav1dStep). sigma = 0.5 is that per-step standard deviation rounded up to one significant digit, about half the reward range (1.05) and ten times the -0.05 step penalty.

onlyDifference: agent.doubleQ = false for dqn, true for double-dqn

budget.unit: environment steps (identical for both algorithms; an episode still running when the budget is reached is not logged as an episode, its length is in summary.partialEpisodeAtBudget)
budget.choice: Unchanged from the control on purpose (same 50000 env steps per run). Drawing the noise adds two uniforms and one log/cos per env step, negligible next to the train step.

agent.epsilonSchedule: multiplied by epsilonDecay after each train() call; epsilonDecay = 0.05^(1/15000), so minEpsilon is reached after 15000 train steps (30 % of the budget)
agent.targetUpdateUnit: train() calls (hard copy of the online weights)
agent.optimizer: adam, mean squared error, 1 epoch per train() call, shuffle off (seeded)

probeStarts.spacing: evenly spaced, identical for every algo, seed and checkpoint

overestimation.estimated: max_a Q_online(s0, a) at each probe start s0
overestimation.observed: discounted Monte-Carlo return (same gamma) of the greedy policy rolled out from s0 on the TRUE reward (meanDiscountedReturn); the env is deterministic, so one rollout is the exact true return of that policy
overestimation.gap: estimated - observed on the TRUE reward (meanGap); positive means the network expects more than its own greedy policy obtains. Overestimation is read against the true return, declared before the runs.
overestimation.reference: optimalDiscountedReturn: return of the optimal policy (always +0.15) from s0
overestimation.measureUnchanged: Same probe starts, same checkpoints every 1000 env steps, same gamma 0.99, same estimated quantity max_a Q_online(s0, a) as the control.
overestimation.observedNoisy: meanDiscountedNoisyReturn: the same greedy rollout with N(0, sigma^2) added to each reward, from its own stream mulberry32(seed * 104729 + globalStep * 9 + probeIndex) (same draws for both algos at equal seed and checkpoint). Logged for reference only.

eval.starts: uniform[0, 0.4] via mulberry32(seed * 17 + 3), as in RL 1
eval.checkpoint: frozen trained policy reloaded in a new process (eval-new-process.json)
eval.replay: greedy (epsilon = 0) episode from position 0.2 for every algo and seed (trained-greedy.json, untrained-greedy.json), same start as the RL 1 replay
eval.reward: greedy evals, replays and episode returns use the true reward; episodes.jsonl also logs noisyReturn (sum of the noisy rewards the agent received)

summary.trueReward: lastMeanReturn, greedyEvalMean and finalQVsReturn are on the true reward; lastMeanNoisyReturn and finalQVsReturn.meanDiscountedNoisyReturn are the noisy counterparts; summary.rewardNoise holds the count, sum, mean and std of the noise actually drawn
